builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Outcome-Mass Alignment: Controlling Length-Dependent Trajectory Influence in Multi-Turn LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: OMA replaces the implicit weighting rule in stepwise group-relative multi-turn RL by computing outcome statistics over unique source trajectories and controlling aggregate objective mass after within-trajectory aggregation, without changing the base optimizer's credit assignment, importance ratios, or clipping. It adds modest accounting complexity and requires tracking trajectory expansion and outcome coupling, but it does not introduce a new training-stage dependency or obvious inference cost. It can fail when expansion does not couple to outcomes, as the paper reports mixed or reversed effects on ordinary WebShop, so gains are workload-dependent rather than universal.
rationale: The method is small enough to validate in a constrained setup, but its benefit depends on expansion-outcome coupling in the target workload, so it should be tested rather than adopted by default.

claims.statement: OMA replaces the implicit weighting rule in stepwise group-relative multi-turn RL by computing outcome statistics over unique source trajectories and controlling aggregate objective mass after within-trajectory aggregation, without changing the base optimizer's credit assignment, importance ratios, or clipping. It adds modest accounting complexity and requires tracking trajectory expansion and outcome coupling, but it does not introduce a new training-stage dependency or obvious inference cost. It can fail when expansion does not couple to outcomes, as the paper reports mixed or reversed effects on ordinary WebShop, so gains are workload-dependent rather than universal.

On ALFWorld GRPO at two model scales, OMA improves matched-horizon endpoint success by 7.0-9.4 percentage points; on WebShop-SOL it improves success nAUC from 0.399 to 0.511, with mixed effects on ordinary WebShop.
